premises.text: Vendors amass and leverage shopping/tracking data while consumers forget purchases—data leverage is one-sided
premises.evidence_span: Those with the vendors are the only ones that can be amassing and leveraging and tracking the data that's out there

premises.text: Forwarding order confirmations into Schwope captures purchases into a consumer account
premises.evidence_span: forward my order confirmations in my inbox to wowat12.com

premises.text: Consumers augment purchase records with why/need/story and control sharing (e.g., friends only)—taste signaling and mindfulness
premises.evidence_span: augmenting the basic purchase data, the stuff that's like the what, the how much sort of thing, with the why

premises.text: History analytics, social share, and Shopify/plugin ingest make shopping data meaningful and compatible with many stores
premises.evidence_span: slice this and mash up this data and show analytics around this data to make it meaningful for the customers

premises.text: Data-out personal RFP: consumers opt-in share selected history with chosen brands/vendors for personalized deals, loyalty, VIP, better search
premises.evidence_span: the data actually gets powerful when the customer can take all that they've amassed and leverage it back for something of value in return

value.text: Give consumers equal leverage with their shopping data for meaningful use and value in return
value.evidence_span: what if the consumers had as much leverage with the data as the vendors do?

causal_links.evidence_span: building tools for consumers to help them make their shopping data more meaningful
leverage it back for something of value in return

notes: Minority Report framing folded into one-sided data problem. Ingest/augment/slice/plugin cascade for data-in product (§4.1.7). Personal RFP split as separately framed data-out vision module that must hold for disruptive value. Retailer 'powered by' talks treated as GTM facet of data-out. ASR Schwope/Schwab/Schwelp kept in spans as present.
